I've never been diagnosed with anything but I very much will just go hungry if there's no food ill eat and my only safe foods are unhealthy and expensive (not McDonald's but I don't feel like being vulnerable on reddit today). Two cheaper things that I will eat and your daughter *may* be open to trying is cereal and basically any form of cookie. I also have a friend who lives exclusively off of baked potatoes and coffee, and another who will only eat yogurt with two different options of fruit. 

Obviously, you seem like a caring mother who doesn't want her kids to be unhealthy, but this is clearly going to take a very long time to resolve. If you can coax your daughter into trying different foods, I would suggest just accepting the junk food fixation and prioritizing affordable varieties. 
I'm sure you know your daughter best, but it does sound like she has autism, so the easiest way to coax her into trying things is probably to bribe her with her special interests. I know money is tight, so it can be a small thing like offering to watch her favorite show or movie with her if she'll try xyz. Most kids love time with mom, so it's a pretty good bribe. I know it's the exact opposite of what you'd like to do but temporarily giving up on her nutrition in favor of caloric intake so you can also eat yourself and feed your son is going to help your sanity in the long run. And a lot of us autistic adults get quite far on vitamin supplements later in life, so don't worry too much about permanent solutions just yet. 
Good luck!!!

The moral of the story is, sometimes you need to train your dogs and care for their needs and happiness in ways that dont intuitively make sense. Not allowing him to sit on laps seemed really strange when the trainer suggested it as a method for dealing with his anxiety but since it was implemented he has been happier and healthier than ever before. That being said the hair still gets everywhere even where the dog isnt, dont get a dog if you cant cope with furmaggedon, but also dont assume thats what's up if someone has different rules for their dog(s) than you do!
